caption: The photographer alone came to R1 200 and I hadn't even budgeted for hair. What did matric dance actually cost your family?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R27 000
p/m salary
Living in Klerksdorp
slides.body:
Female, 43
Married, one teen (18) finishing matric this year
Job: Occupational therapist, public hospital
Net salary: R27 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: Nearly paid off. That's the only reason this month still balances.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of three, plus the extra with a matriculant who's never home to eat it
slides.body: I buy for three and cook for two most nights.

slides.title: Matric dance costs
slides.includes: Dress alterations, a hired suit for her date, hair and make-up, photos
slides.body: I budgeted R1 500. The photographer alone was R1 200 of that.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: The school run ends this year. I haven't worked out what replaces it in the budget.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Family plan, one hospital admission excess still being paid off
slides.body: Working in a hospital doesn't make the medical aid bill any smaller.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & insurance, electricity, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, savings
slides.body: Six things that keep running whether or not it's a matric year.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R27 000. The matric dance was one month's spend. The relief afterwards was worth more than the number.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what the year would actually cost
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and budgeted the matric dance as its own category.

Seeing the photographer against the dress against the suit hire made the number make sense instead of just hurting.

No bank login needed.
